writeup.p: The swing packet is the client's arm-swing notice to the server. C0APacketAnimation carries no payload: in 1.8.9 both readPacketData and writePacketData are no-ops, so the wire cost is a single packet id byte (0x0A). EntityPlayerSP.swingItem() fires it at the start of each swing cycle under the isSwingInProgress guard, and the server echoes the action to every tracked player as S0BPacketAnimation with animation id 0. Because the packet is unauthenticated action signaling, its only real content is timing: when it arrives and how often.

Server side, NetHandlerPlayServer.processAnimation calls markPlayerActive() then swingItem() on the EntityPlayerMP. The first resets the idle counter used by the player-list AFK kick logic; the second advances the entity's swing animation and broadcasts S0BPacketAnimation to all trackers. Client side, swingItem() sends the packet once per swing cycle, so one swing equals one packet in vanilla. Mining, attacking and block placement all route through the same swing; the attack itself is a separate C02PacketUseEntity.

Five distinct uses appear in the corpus. Scaffold modules send C0A after every onPlayerRightClick3d placement so the server sees a swing matching the block place (Memeware, Nekoware, Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x, Sigma, Tenacity). KillAura-family modules send it in place of swingItem() when the local animation must stay off (Spicy Killaura noSwing mode, Rise 5.99 Aura alwaysSwing). Stealer modules swing before opening chests in Nearby mode. Rise 6.x treats C0A as a swing state bit in BadPacketsComponent and sends it from velocity and flight modes to satisfy attack heuristics. Tenacity Crasher floods 2000 to 10000 C0A packets per motion tick.

The packet is empty and the server broadcasts the swing to every tracker, so flooding multiplies server work per byte: Tenacity's Crasher pushes up to 10000 per tick to exhaust the server. Swing rate is also a heuristic input: anti-cheats pair C0A with C02PacketUseEntity to count real attacks, which is why velocity modes send C0A before attackEntity (GrimReduceVelocity). A spoofed swing is always safe: the packet carries no position, timestamp or sequence, so the server cannot verify it, only count it.

overview: The empty swing packet. Scaffold, KillAura, Stealer and velocity modules inject C0A to keep server-side animation consistent with spoofed actions, Rise 6.x tracks it as a bad-packet state bit, and Tenacity's Crasher weaponizes its zero-payload cheapness by flooding thousands per tick.
server_handling: processAnimation is two calls: markPlayerActive() resets the idle-tick counter that protects against AFK kicks, then swingItem() plays the arm animation and broadcasts S0BPacketAnimation to tracked players. There is no validation on the packet itself: no cooldown, no rate limit, no payload. Any count per tick is accepted and echoed.
protocol_notes: The class is a pure marker: readPacketData and writePacketData are no-ops, so a swing costs one VarInt id byte on the wire. The client sends it from EntityPlayerSP.swingItem() once per swing cycle, guarded by isSwingInProgress. The serverbound id 0x0A maps to the arm-swing animation id 0 in the S0BPacketAnimation broadcast. Timing is the only signal: anti-cheats derive swing rate and attack cadence from packet arrival, not from content.
anticheat_landscape: Attack anti-cheats count C0A arrivals relative to C02PacketUseEntity: swings without attacks are tolerated (mining, air swings), but bursts of swings with no C03 or C02 between them read as scaffold or autoclicker activity. Rise 6.x BadPacketsComponent explicitly tracks swing as a flag and resets it on the next C03PacketPlayer; other modules query that flag before sending spoofed actions. Flooding C0A trips server-side packet-rate limits long before any movement check.

modules.name: Scaffold
modules.purpose: Send a swing with each block placement so the server sees a human-looking arm action alongside the C08 place packet.
modules.how_it_works: In the post phase of UpdateEvent, after onPlayerRightClick3d returns true, push a raw C0APacketAnimation into the send queue. The pre phase computes the placement target and rotations; the swing is fired only when the placement actually succeeded.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent post phase; swing follows the placement call, not a packet event.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Harmless: it matches vanilla placing behavior (swing accompanies the block place). The flag surface is the placement rate, not the swing.
modules.variations: Nekoware's Scaffold is byte-for-byte the same pattern. Rise 5.99 sends via PacketUtil.sendPacket. Rise 6.x Scaffold sends at its line ~752 with PacketUtil.send. Sigma sends via sendQueue in two code paths (lines ~431 and ~1089). Tenacity ScaffoldModule sends at line ~201 via addToSendQueue.

modules.name: KillAura / Aura
modules.purpose: Swing server-side while controlling the local animation. Spicy's noSwing mode sends the packet instead of swingItem() so the arm does not visibly swing client-side.
modules.how_it_works: On the attack timer elapse, if noSwing is enabled, push new C0APacketAnimation() into the send queue and then send C02PacketUseEntity ATTACK; otherwise call swingItem() locally. Rise 5.99 Aura sends C0A when alwaysSwing is on and the raytrace failed, faking swings at out-of-range targets. Rise 6.x KillAura tracks C0A in onPacketSend to set its swing state bit, consumed by auto-block delay logic.
modules.vanilla_hook: Attack timer in an update event; C0A is constructed directly, never via swingItem().
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Swinging without a matching attack is legal (air swings), so the noSwing swap is low risk. The Rise 5.99 alwaysSwing variant adds swings at out-of-range targets, which inflates swing rate and can trip rate heuristics.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 implements it as Aura with an alwaysSwing setting. Rise 6.x KillAura consumes C0A as a state signal. Sigma's Killaura imports C0A but its corpus hit is import-only. Spicy's memes modules (CsgoSpinbot, YawAndPitchSpoof and friends) match C0A in packet events to replay or rotate around swings.

modules.name: Stealer
modules.purpose: Chest stealing. Sends C0A before the right-click that opens a nearby chest, mimicking an interaction swing.
modules.how_it_works: Nearby mode scans a 3-block radius each delay tick; for every chest not yet emptied, PacketUtil.sendPacket(new C0APacketAnimation()) fires, then onPlayerRightClick opens it. Emptied positions are cleared on S08PacketPlayerPosLook and on enable.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent; swing is sent via PacketUtil.sendPacket before onPlayerRightClick.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Invisible to anti-cheats; interaction order (swing then use) is exactly what a player produces.
modules.variations: Nekoware v1 private ships the same module with the same C0A send.

modules.name: BadPacketsComponent
modules.purpose: A shared state tracker, not a user module: flags swing=true on any outgoing C0A and resets all flags on the next C03PacketPlayer. Other modules call BadPacketsComponent.bad() to decide whether spoofed packets are safe to send.
modules.how_it_works: PacketSendEvent at VERY_HIGH priority sets one boolean per packet family: slot (C09), swing (C0A), attack (C02), block (C08/C07), inventory (C0E/C16 OPEN_INVENTORY/C0D). C03PacketPlayer clears everything. Modules gate spoofed sends on bad() so they never fire mid-sequence.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The component is defensive: it prevents the client from emitting overlapping action packets that anti-cheats read as impossible sequences.
modules.variations: Identical in Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4. It is also the gate for the C0D close in WatchdogDisabler and the C0A send in GrimReduceVelocity.

modules.name: Crasher
modules.purpose: Lag or kill the server by flooding zero-payload swings, exploiting the server's per-packet broadcast cost.
modules.how_it_works: On every MotionEvent, loop 2000 iterations (Vanilla mode) or 10000 (Boom mode) pushing new C0APacketAnimation() into the send queue in a single tick.
modules.vanilla_hook: MotionEvent; packets are queued via addToSendQueue, not a packet event.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Trips packet-rate limits instantly on any server with them; this is a grief tool, not a bypass.
modules.variations: None in the corpus; Tenacity also lists C0A in its PacketUtil as one of the packet types that bypass the send queue filter.

modules.name: GrimReduceVelocity
modules.purpose: Pair a swing with the velocity-reduction attack so the attack sequence looks legitimate to anti-cheats.
modules.how_it_works: On PreUpdateEvent, if within 14 ticks of taking velocity and BadPacketsComponent.bad() is false, send C0APacketAnimation then call playerController.attackEntity on the nearest target. The swing precedes the attack so the server sees a clean swing-attack pair.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The swing makes the velocity attack read as a normal hit; the real flag surface is the velocity reduction itself, not the swing.
modules.variations: The same swing-before-action pattern appears across the Rise 6.x velocity and flight tree: AACVelocity, WatchdogPredictionVelocity, WatchdogLongJump, BlockFlight, UnKnownAC, AntiFireBall, Clutch. Rise 6.1.30's AntiFireBall uses PacketUtil.sendNoEvent instead of send.

general_hooks: PacketSendEvent is the filter surface: Rise 5.99 AutoGap checks instanceof C0APacketAnimation to time eating, Freecam/FreeCam whitelist C0A in packet passthrough lists, and Spicy CsgoSpinbot and YawAndPitchSpoof match it in packet events. Tenacity PacketUtil counts C0A among packet types exempt from its send queue.
client_variations: Older clients (Memeware, Nekoware, Sigma, Spicy, Tenacity) push via mc.thePlayer.sendQueue.addToSendQueue; Rise 5.99 uses PacketUtil.sendPacket; Rise 6.x uses PacketUtil.send and sendNoEvent. The Rise 6.1.30 AntiFireBall uses sendNoEvent where 6.2.4 uses send.
